original_test_intent: Have an authorized operator verify that SOL maps to the intended ttyS0 console at 115200 baud, displays live readable output and supports exact safe bidirectional copy/paste.
original_method: Independently verify BMC/SUT/ttyS0/SOL channel and serial parameters; open the protected live console; visually confirm target and readable output; at an approved safe prompt round-trip a unique harmless marker in both directions while recording character order, line endings, focus and latency; close and verify no session lock or configuration drift.
manual_activity: An authorized operator verifies ttyS0 routing and focus, judges live output, performs the harmless copy/paste round trip and confirms clean closure; automation may only prepare and capture evidence.
required_inputs: Unique harmless marker and line-ending oracle
safety_requirements: Do not substitute SSH or a sensor query
Verify target, channel and focus before input
Never paste credentials, secrets or executable commands
Account for newline and terminal escape handling
Stop on garbling, duplication, loss or wrong prompt
Preserve logs and never auto-retry ambiguous interaction
agent_execution_scope: Verify session close and unchanged configuration
engineer_actions: Confirm ttyS0/SOL target and safe prompt
Visually judge live output and focus

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The TEMP_UBB_FRONT SSH/sensor command is unrelated to ttyS0, SOL, baud or interactive copy/paste and cannot be used for this variant.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: MANUAL ONLY: open the verified ttyS0-backed SOL session at approved 115200 settings and let the operator perform an exact harmless-marker round trip at a safe text surface.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The ttyS0, 115200, bidirectional copy/paste and 20/20-minute interactive scope are retained; no unrelated sensor work or log clearing is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record channel/serial settings, redacted live console identity, source and returned marker bytes, line-ending transformations, focus/latency/drop behavior, session start/end and lock-free cleanup.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact route verification, a non-executable test marker, byte-level round-trip evidence and controlled session lifecycle.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Readable output alone does not prove local-to-console paste, console-to-local copy or character fidelity; a sensor command proves none of them.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Terminal programs may normalize CR/LF or clipboard encodings; approved normalization rules are needed so benign transformations are not mistaken for loss.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define the exact ttyS0/SOL mapping, expected BIOS/OS console state and allowed line-ending normalization. The later duplicate-code row remains a separate variant and must not be merged by code.
expected_evidence: Target identity, ttyS0/SOL mapping and 115200/flow-control/encoding settings
Focus, latency, garbling, duplication, loss and line-ending checklist
Preserved SOL/BMC/SEL/OS audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, procedure and criteria consistently target ttyS0 SOL and copy/paste. DeepSeek's unrelated sensor content is a reference mismatch, while the duplicate code is kept variant-specific.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Mapping, parameters, operator and safe prompt are obtainable inputs. A run reports BLOCKED if the target console or harmless interaction cannot be established safely.

review_improvement: Replaces an unrelated sensor check with the actual operator-attended ttyS0 route, live readability and exact bidirectional clipboard evidence required by the source.
independent_technical_reasoning: A clipboard action can append a newline or terminal control sequence, turning test text into a command at a shell or bootloader. Therefore the safe surface and marker contents matter as much as visible characters. Both directions must be checked separately because terminal capture and paste paths use different encoding and flow-control mechanisms.
